question.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2-t,\,{p}_{2}(t)=3-2{t}^{2},\,q(t)=3t-4{t}^{2}.
$$

If $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2-t)+{x}_{2}(3-2{t}^{2}) & =3t-4{t}^{2} \\ (2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2})-{x}_{1}t-2{x}_{2}{t}^{2} & =3t-4{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}=3 \\ -2{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=3 \\ 3{x}_{2}=6 \\ -2{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ From the  first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-3.$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3+2=-1.$
